'''''Quercus'' × ''rosacea''''', the '''hybrid oak''',<ref name=BSBI>{{cite web | title=Hybrid Oak ''Quercus petraea × robur'' = ''Q. × ⁠rosacea'' Bechst. | website=PlantAtlas | url=https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.1y2 | access-date=2025-04-29}}</ref> is a naturally occurring hybrid species of [[Quercus|oak]] native to central and northern Europe.<ref name="POWO"/> It is a hybrid between sessile oak ''[[Quercus petraea]]'', and pedunculate oak ''[[Quercus robur]]'', found where their ranges overlap. As a fertile hybrid, it is morphologically variable, but in general the traits are intermediate between those of the parents.<ref name=BSBI/>

A thin section of a ''Q.''{{nbsp}}×{{nbsp}}''rosacea'' specimen was used by artist-in-residence Tania Kovats to create a monumental work called TREE for the [[Ceilings of the Natural History Museum, London|ceiling of the Mezzanine]] of the [[Natural History Museum, London]] in celebration of the bicentennial of Charles Darwin's birth.<ref>{{cite journal |last1= Hellström|first1= Nils Petter|title= The tree as evolutionary icon: TREE in the Natural History Museum, London (William T. Stearn Prize 2010)|url= http://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:uu:diva-187297|journal= Archives of Natural History|volume= 38|issue= 1|pages= 1–17|doi=10.3366/anh.2011.0001 |pmid= 21560437|year= 2011}}</ref>
